An 'escalation count' therefore names an object the current process does not define, so no structural count against a record shape is possible. findings.statement: The marker-transition method structurally cannot see a [u] integration verdict. That verdict is recorded beneath the node while the node's own marker stays [x], so a method reading marker state reports 'no escalation' for a Task that was in fact handed to human authority twice. Two of the four genuine escalations (0040-09, 0044-01) are invisible to it by construction, not by accident.

0037-07 escalated and left no marker trace on main at all. The [u] was set and resolved without a first-parent transition surviving, so even a perfect marker reader would miss it. Marker history is not a complete record of escalation.

The lexical measure's 9 is not an escalation count with noise; 5 of its 9 hits are not escalations, and one (0037-37) matches text that explicitly forbids escalating. A keyword measure cannot distinguish a state from a requirement about that state, from the topic of the Task, from the word's negation.

The contract asks for an escalation count for which the active process defines no countable object. There is no conforming escalation-record shape in force; the only defined shapes are the [u] marker (which misses integration verdicts and prose-only cases) and the [u] integration verdict (which is defined for integration only). This is a defect of the process 0039-01 exists to define, and is carried into its requirements rather than resolved by picking whichever proxy reads better.

In this population the two automated measures happen to bracket the adjudicated value (1 <= 4 <= 9), but that bracketing is observed, not guaranteed: an escalation recorded with none of the keywords would fall outside the upper bound too. A bracket of width 9 around a value of 4 is not a measurement, and its endpoints must not be reported as bounds.
